question.text: In case of an indirect acquisition where none of the Regulation 5 parameters are met, within how many working days must the public announcement under SEBI SAST Regulations 2011 be made?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SAST, for an indirect acquisition where none of the Regulation 5 parameters (which would otherwise treat it as a direct acquisition) are met, the public announcement must be made within 4 working days of the trigger. For the generic case of agreeing to acquire shares/voting rights/control, the public announcement is made on the date of the agreement itself. The Trap: 2 working days is too short and may be confused with stock-exchange disclosure timelines under LODR. 7 or 10 working days relate to other SAST timelines (DPS publication and minimum tendering period respectively). Note: Always check whether the transaction is a direct or indirect acquisition and, for indirect acquisitions, whether any Regulation 5 parameter is met — the trigger date for the public announcement is materially different in each case.
